suspects.name: Unidentified Motorist
suspects.description: A driver possibly present near the crash site in the window before it was reported.

related_persons.name: Trooper Daniels
related_persons.description: Made brief roadside contact with Bryce hours before the crash was discovered.

related_persons.name: Tow Operator (Reyes Towing)
related_persons.description: Recovered the wrecked vehicle from the roadside.

timeline.event: Bryce leaves a gathering acting erratically
Bryce calls Sarah; the call is described as confused and rambling
Bryce contacts roadside assistance for a flat tire
Trooper Daniels makes brief contact with Bryce on the roadside
Final outgoing call, to Tom Ridley, lasting nine seconds
Vehicle found crashed off the roadway; no trace of Bryce at the scene

evidence.name: Roadside Assistance Call Log
evidence.description: Timestamped record of Bryce's call requesting help with a flat tire.

evidence.name: Trooper Contact Report
evidence.description: Daniels' report describing Bryce as disoriented but coherent enough to decline further assistance.

evidence.name: Final Call Transcript Summary
evidence.description: Nine-second call to Tom Ridley; no words are recovered, only background sound analysis.

evidence.name: Vehicle Forensic Report
evidence.description: Establishes the crash mechanics but not what happened to Bryce afterward — the vehicle proves a crash occurred, not a disappearance method.

evidence.name: K9 Scent Trail Report
evidence.description: Tracking dogs follow a scent trail a short distance from the vehicle before it ends abruptly near a roadway.

evidence.name: Unaccounted Tire Impressions
evidence.description: Additional tire impressions near the crash site that do not match Bryce's vehicle or the tow truck, and were never matched to a known vehicle.

evidence.name: Behavioral/Substance Notes
evidence.description: Compiled notes on Bryce's erratic state that evening; heavily emphasized by the case AI as the default explanation for everything that follows.

puzzles.name: Last Six Hours
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the final sequence of calls, stops, and contacts.

puzzles.name: Roadside Stop
puzzles.description: Separate verified observations of Bryce's state from after-the-fact interpretation.

puzzles.name: Police Encounter
puzzles.description: Compare what Trooper Daniels actually observed against the narrative that was built afterward.

directly_observed: Bryce was upright, ambulatory, and verbally responsive
narrative_added_afterward: That the encounter proves intent to disappear
observed_vs_narrative.reasoning: The report itself is narrow and behavioral. Its later use as proof of a specific motive is an interpretive leap, not a fact in the record.

puzzles.name: Route Gap
puzzles.description: Identify the unexplained stretch of time and movement between the roadside stop and the crash.

puzzles.name: Crash Scene
puzzles.description: Determine precisely what the vehicle evidence establishes, and what it leaves open.

puzzles.name: Scent Trail
puzzles.description: Examine the significance and the limitations of where the scent trail ends.

puzzles.name: Final Reconstruction
puzzles.description: The player must hold multiple competing hypotheses simultaneously rather than collapsing to the AI-favored explanation.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Repeatedly resurfaces Bryce's substance use and emotional state as the simplest explanation, discouraging further inquiry into the unmatched tire impressions.
puzzles.design_constraint: The puzzle must not force a single resolution. The case remains genuinely open: voluntary disappearance, undiscovered self-harm, and third-party intervention must all remain live possibilities that the evidence does not fully close off.

hypotheses.statement: Bryce voluntarily walked away from the crash and disappeared intentionally.
Bryce died by undiscovered self-harm near the crash site.
Bryce's genuine crisis was real, but it became cover for an unrelated third party's involvement.
The critical unknown event happened before the crash, not after it.
